claim_being_audited: Whether certifying the model for launch is compliant and evidentially supported despite a known 1.4-point performance gap in the loan-modification support segment and an unresolved disclosure/materiality question.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence satisfies the policy threshold.
Treat a weakness as material if it affects a contractual customer segment, protected segment, or named launch use case.
Do not treat product labels like non-core or low-volume as dispositive where customer commitments or pending legal review exist.
Require either resolution of the disclosure issue or approved risk acceptance before treating the certification basis as fully supported.
evidence_requests: Final legal determination on whether the gap must be disclosed.
Any approved risk-acceptance record covering this named launch use case.
The operative certification or launch-approval document showing how material limitations are handled.
Direct evidence showing whether certification includes disclosure of the named-segment limitation.
specific_concerns: The admissible record supports aggregate readiness and monitoring discipline, but not a clean policy basis for certification without resolving the materiality/disclosure issue.
The policy text says product labels such as non-core or low-volume do not resolve materiality when the affected segment is named in customer commitments or named launch use cases.
The record says the affected loan-modification support segment is named in two lender rollout commitments, which cuts against treating the weakness as immaterial.
Legal review is still open, so a required policy predicate appears unresolved.
No approved risk acceptance or final disclosure determination is identified in the available evidence summary.
unsupported_claims: Any claim that the disputed weakness is immaterial is not adequately supported by the available admissible evidence.
Any claim that nondisclosure is policy-compliant is not supported on the present record.
Any claim that aggregate readiness alone satisfies the disclosure/materiality requirement is unsupported by the cited policy text.
